* * * *
 JUDGMENT

The petitioners have filed this petition claiming compensation of Rs.50,00,000/ for the death of Sri.Jayaramanna, in the road traffic accident occurred on 24.04.2022.
02.

The brief facts are as under: It is submitted that on 24.04.2022 at about 05.30 p.m one Jayaramanna was going on his TVS Moped XL bearing No.KA64H5720 on the left side of the road and when he came near the land of Doddeeranna at Gondihalli Mutt, in between Gondihalli and Lakkanahalli Road, at that time the rider of Royal Enfield Bullet Bike bearing No.KA05LC 5006 came in rash and negligent manner and dashed against TVS XL of said Jayaramanna.

Due to this said Jayaramanna had sustained grievous injuries and he was shifted to Government hospital,
Sira.
That after first aid he was shifted to Government hospital, Tumakuru and then he was shifted to Victoria hospital, Bengaluru.
But (SCCH3) 4 M.V.C.No.5754/2022 inspite of best treatment he had succumbed to the injuries on 30.04.2022 at about 03.17 p.m.
Then the Post mortem was conducted and dead body was handed over to the petitioners.

The petitioners have shifted the dead body in hired car to their native place and conducted funeral ceremony by spending Rs.1,05,000/
towards medical expenses, transportation charges, funeral and other incidental charges.
Due to the death of Jayaramanna, the petitioners being the wives are suffering from pain and sufferings and lost love and affection of their husband.

That the deceased prior to the accident was hale and healthy Bhimakka vs Cholamandalam General Insurance Co., ... on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129579109/
2 and was doing agriculture, sheep rearing and business and earning Rs.50,000/ p.m.

sentences.text: The accident occurred is solely due to the rash and negligent riding of rider of Royal Enfield Bike.
A criminal case was also registered against rider of Royal Enfield Bike.
The respondent No.1 is the insurer and the respondent No.2 is the owner of the said offending Bike.
Hence, both respondents are liable to pay the compensation.
Hence this petition.
03. After service of notice, the respondents No.1 and 2 have appeared through their counsel and filed written statement.

(SCCH3) 5 M.V.C.No.5754/2022 04. The averments of the written statement of respondent No.1 is as under: This respondent has issued policy of insurance in favour of respondent No.2 in respect of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA 05LC5006 for own damage from 23.01.2021 to 22.01.2022.
The period of insurance for third party from 23.01.2021 to 22.01.2026.
But liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.
The respondent No.2 has not intimated about the accident.

The respondent No.2 has knowingly entrusted the vehicle to the rider who had no valid and effective driving licence to ride the vehicle and hence there is breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
The petitioners are not the legal heirs and dependents on the deceased.

This respondent denies manner of accident, age, occupation,
income and expenses incurred by the plaintiff for the deceased.
The accident took place due to the negligent act of the deceased only and not due to the rider of Motor Cycle.
The bike is not involved in this accident.
The claim of the petitioners are highly excessive and exaggerated and hence prays to dismiss the petition.
05. The averments of the written statement of respondent No.2 is as under: (SCCH3) 6 M.V.C.No.5754/2022
This respondent has denied manner of accident, age, avocation, income and expenses incurred by the petitioners for the deceased.
The accident did not occurred due to the negligence of bike rider but it is due to the negligence of deceased himself.
The Bike bearing No.KA 05LC5006 was duly insured with respondent No.1 and the policy was in force on the date of accident.
The said motorcycle was having valid documents and the rider is also having valid driving licence.
Hence this respondent is not liable to pay compensation and respondent No.1 is only liable to pay the compensation and prays to dismiss the petition with costs.
06. In order to prove the case, the petitioner No.1 was got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 15 documents as Ex.P.1 to 15 and closed their side.
07. By way of rebuttal, the Assistant Manager - Legal of the respondent No.1 got examined himself as RW.1 and got marked 2 documents as Ex.R.1 and 2 and closed their side.

08. Heard arguments from both sides.
09.
Based on the aforesaid pleadings, the following issues have been framed:

sentences.text: 01. Whether petitioners prove that they are the LRs/dependants of deceased Sri.Jayaramanna S/o Lingegowda?

02. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Sri.Jayaramanna S/o Lingegowda died in RTA arising out of the accident alleged to have been taken place on 24.04.2022 at about 05.30 p.m.,near the land of Doddeerappa, GandhihalliLakkanahalli Road, Gandihalli Mutt, Hulikunte Hobli, Sira Taluk, Tumakuru, due to negligent act of riding of the Bike bearing registration No.KA05LC 5006 by its rider as alleged in the petition?
03. Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04 . What order or award?

10. My findings on the aforesaid issues are as under: Issue No.1 In affirmative Issue No.2 In affirmative Issue No.3 In partly Affirmative Issue No.4 As per final order for the following:
 (SCCH3) 8 M.V.C.No.5754/2022  REASONS 11. Issues No.1 and 2: These issues will be taken at one stretch for my consideration in order to avoid repetition of facts as they are inter related with each other.

It is the grievance of the petitioners that the deceased Jayaramanna died in road traffic accident which took place on 24.04.2022 due to the rash and negligent manner riding of Bike bearing No.
KA05LC5006.
Further they have contended that they are the legal heirs and dependents of deceased.
Due to the death of deceased, the petitioners have lost their bread earner and facing financial problems and mental stress.
Hence, they have claimed compensation.
12. Per contra, the same was denied by respondents No.1 and 2 and contended that the accident did not took place due to the negligence of rider of bike but due to negligence of deceased himself.
Hence the petitioners are not entitled for compensation.
13. In order to prove this, the petitioner No.1 was got examined herself as PW.1 by reiterating all the (SCCH3) 9 M.V.C.No.5754/2022 averments of the petition in her affidavit.
The PW.1 in her cross examination admitted that "The moped in which my husband was proceeding belongs to him.
I can produce Driving licence of my husband.
I have not seen the accident.
Immediately after the accident my husband was taken to Sira hospital and then shifted to Government hospital, Tumakuru and then shifted to Victoria hospital.
I can produce treatment records of my husband.
That my husband was admitted as inpatient for seven days.
That my husband was alone proceeding in the moped.
That my husband had two wives.
That I had no children.

That another wife of my husband had one Bhimakka vs Cholamandalam General Insurance Co., ... on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129579109/
4 daughter.

entities.text: Bhimakka vs Cholamandalam General Insurance Co.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The said daughter of deceased was married.
I can produce ration card.
I can produce the Aadhaar card of my deceased husband.
That my husband was doing agriculture.
It is true that I have not produced any document to show that my husband had land and doing agriculture.
That I and another wife of deceased are residing together.
It is true that I and another wife of deceased were working.
That I was earning Rs.20,000/, Rs.25,000/ and Rs.50,000/ per month.
Even the another wife of deceased is also earning Rs.10,000/, Rs.15,000/ and Rs.25,000/ per month.
I do not know for which (SCCH3) 10 M.V.C.No.5754/2022 purpose Ex.P.12 and 13 were produced".
The PW.1 had denied all other suggestions of the respondent No.1 counsel.
The PW.1 had not seen the accident.
She had deposed based on the available documents on record.
14. Per contra, the Assistnat Manager  Legal of the respondent No.1 was got examined himself as RW.1 by reiterating all the averments of the written statement in his affidavit.
Further in his cross examination the RW.1 has admitted that "That I am working in the company since 15 days.
I am aware about the facts of this case.
It is true that I am giving evidence based upon police records.
It is true that as on the date of accident the bike bearing registration No.KA5LC5006 was insured by our company ".

The RW.1 has got marked Authorization letter and copy of Policy as per Ex.R.1 and 2.
15.
Further in support of the case, the PW.1 got marked entire police documents as per Ex.P.1 to 11.

On perusal of these documents, it is clear that the concerned I.O after investigation have filed Charge sheet against rider of Bike bearing No.KA05LC5006 for the alleged offences punishable U/s 279, 304(A) of IPC and U/Sec.181 and 187 of IMV Act for the reason that the rider of Bike had no valid driving licence at (SCCH3) 11 M.V.C.No.5754/2022 the time of accident to ride such type of vehicle.

Further the said rider after causing the accident did not provided first aid treatment to the injured, not informed about the accident to the Police and had not stopped the vehicle and fled away from the accident spot.
As per Ex.P.3 the concerned I.O have stated that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of bike rider only.
16. It is true that the respondent No.2 had violated the terms and conditions of the policy as he had entrusted the vehicle to the rider who had no valid and effective driving licence.
But the respondents have not proved that the accident has not occurred due to the negligence of their insured bike rider.
Even there are no supportive documents on their behalf in this regard.
17. Further the petitioners have produced mahazar, sketch and IMV report as per Ex.P.4, 5 and 8 which supports the version of the petitioners.
So in absence of any documents the contention of the respondent No.1 is not acceptable one.
The respondent No.2 has not whispered anything in this regard.

18. Further the petitioners in order to prove that they are the legal heirs and dependents of the (SCCH3) 12 M.V.C.No.5754/2022 deceased have produced Notarized copy of Aadhaar cards of themselves as per Ex.P.14 and 15.
So, on basis of these documents, I am of opinion that the petitioners No.1 and 2 who are the wives of the deceased can be considered as dependents and legal heirs of deceased.

Hence with the available documents I am of opinion that the petitioners have proved that the husband of the petitioners died in the accident caused by the bike rider due to his Bhimakka vs Cholamandalam General Insurance Co., ... on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129579109/
5 rash and negligent riding.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, I answered issues No.1 and 2 in affirmative.
19. Issue No.3

: As per above findings, it is clear that the accident took place due to negligent driving of the offending rider of bike and the husband of the petitioners died while taking treatment.
Hence the petitioners No.1 and 2 being the dependents of deceased are entitled for compensation as under:
a) Loss of dependency:- The petitioners submitted that the deceased was aged about 79 years as on the date of accident.
To prove the same, they have not produced any documents.
Hence the age mentioned in medical documents can be considered.

According to Post mortem report marked at Ex.P.7 the (SCCH3) 13 M.V.C.No.5754/2022 age of the deceased is mentioned as 80 years at the time of accident and the same is considered for calculating the compensation.
So, as per Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 the multiplier applicable is "05" and the same is considered.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In order to prove the income of the deceased, the petitioners have produced Invoice and Bill issued by Onion, Potato merchants and commission agents as per Ex.P.12 and 13, except these documents the petitioners have not produced any other relevant documents or examined the author of these documents to prove that the deceased was earning Rs.50,000/ p.m. Hence in the absence of such,
it is just and proper to consider the income as per Minimum Wages Act by considering the deceased as unskilled worker which comes to Rs.13,311/ p.m. Since the deceased has left two dependents, as per Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 if the dependents are 2 to 3, then personal deduction is to be 1/3rd.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence, in this case 1/3rd deduction has to be done towards personal expenses.

So, after deduction of 1/3rd (Rs.4,437/), then the income comes to Rs.8,874/.
The petitioners have stated that apart from the deceased there are no one to look after the petitioners.

But as per Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 the petitioners are not entitled for future prospects as the deceased is above 60 years at the time of his death.

entities.text: Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hence the petitioners are entitled for Rs.8,874 x 12 x 5 = Rs.5,32,440/ under this head.
b) Loss of estate and funeral expenses:

Since it is settled law in National Insurance Company Ltd.,
Vs Pranay Sethi and others case in AIR 2017 SC 5157 that the dependents would be entitled for loss of estate to the extent of Rs.15,000/ and funeral expenses to the extent of Rs.15,000/, as such I award the same.
c) Loss of consortium:

In this case the petitioners No.1 and 2 being the wives of the deceased are entitled for Rs.40,000/ each towards spousal consortium as per Judgment of Hon'ble Supreme (SCCH3) 15 M.V.C.No.5754/2022 Court in United India Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs Satinder Kaur @
Satwinder Kaur & Ors case and Magma General Insurance Company case in (2018) 18 SCC 130.
Bhimakka vs Cholamandalam General Insurance Co., ... on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129579109/
6 20.

Satwinder Kaur & Ors

sentences.text:
Thus the petitioners are entitled for compensation under the following heads:
1.Loss of dependency Rs.5,32,440/
2.Loss of estate 15,000/
3.Towards spousal consortium 80,000/ (for petitioners No.1 and 2)
4.Transportation of dead body 15,000/ and funeral expenses Total Rs.6,42,440/
21.
Regarding liability: As held on above issues the respondents No.1 failed to prove their defence.
The respondent No.1 has admit the policy and it is in force on the date of accident.
But as per the Charge sheet the rider of Bike who had caused accident did not possess valid driving licence at the time of accident.
The respondent No.2 being the owner had violated the terms of the policy by allowing the rider of bike to ride it without having driving licence.
It is true that the respondent No.2 has violated the terms (SCCH3) 16 M.V.C.No.5754/2022 of the policy.

But this is not a ground to exonerate the liability fastened on the respondent No.1.
22.

The respondent No.1 has relied upon decision reported in: a. M.F.A.No.6154/2019 - Hemalatha @ Hema @ Hemavathi and others V/s Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd., and another - It is observed that the insured will not be indemnified if the vehicle is used otherwise than in accordance with law.
23.

entities.text: Hemalatha @ Hema @ Hemavathi and others V/s Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: At this juncture I would like to rely upon decisions reported in a. Civil appeal No. 6902/21 - Kurvan Ansari V/s Shyam Kishore Murmu - It is observed that the entire compensation shall be paid to the claimants as it is open for the insurance company to recover it from the owner when the driver not possessed valid driving licence.

entities.text: Kurvan Ansari V/s Shyam Kishore Murmu
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: b. 2019 ACJ 713 - Gurmail singh V/s Bajaj Allianz General insurance Co., Ltd.,  It is observed that the insurance company has to satisfy the award and then to recover the same from the owner.

entities.text: Gurmail singh V/s Bajaj Allianz General insurance Co., Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: c. National insurance company V/s Swaran Singh - (2004) 3 SCC 297

entities.text: National insurance company V/s Swaran Singh - (2004) 3 SCC 297
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: - It is observed that when there is no valid driving licence in order to protect the rights of the claimants it is just and proper to ask the insurance company to deposit the amount.
The recovery of the same from the owner of the vehicle.
d. Pappu V/s Vinod kumar lamba (2018) 3 SCC 208 - It is observed that when there is no driving licence the insurer has to pay compensation to claimants with liberty to recover it from the owner.

entities.text: Pappu V/s Vinod kumar lamba (2018) 3 SCC 208
entities.label: PRECEDENT

7 e.

sentences.text: It is observed that the insurer is liable to pay to the third party and recover from the insured even if there is breach of any conditions.

24. Therefore under these circumstances, I just feel it proper for the fault committed by the rider of the bike by riding it in rash and negligent manner and caused injuries without holding driving licence the petitioners cannot be made to suffer.

As this is a beneficial legislation I am of opinion that as on the date of accident as the policy was valid, the respondent No.1 shall pay the compensation to the petitioners and then to recover it from the respondent No.2.

Hence in the instant case looking into the facts (SCCH3) 18 M.V.C.No.5754/2022 and circumstances of case the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation eventhough there is no valid driving licence by the offending rider.

The Insurance Company i.e., respondent No.1 has to pay the compensation to the petitioners and then to recover the same from the respondent No.2.
25.
With regard to apportionment is concerned, petitioners No.1 and 2 being the wives of the deceased are equally entitled for 50% each of the amount awarded.
Hence, the issue No.3 is answered in partly affirmative.
26. Issue No.4:

In view of my findings on issues No.1 to 3 as above and with regard to awarding the interest is concerned, the petitioners are entitled for simple interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till deposit.
As such I proceed to pass the following: ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for Rs.6,42,440/ (Six lakhs forty two thousand four hundred and (SCCH3) 19 M.V.C.No.5754/2022 forty only) as compensation with interest at 6% p.a from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

However in view of having valid insurance - the respondent No.1 shall deposit the same within time stipulated under section 168(3) of M.V. Act and then to recover from the respondent No.2.
On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, petitioners No.1 and 2 are equally entitled for 50% each of compensation as awarded.
Out of the share amount of petitioners No.1 and 2 along with interest accrued, entire amount shall be released to them through Epayment on proper identification without any further proceedings.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.

opennyai_summary.facts:
The respondent No.2 has knowingly entrusted the vehicle to the rider who had no valid and effective driving licence to ride the vehicle and hence there is breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
The petitioners are not the legal heirs and dependents on the deceased.
The accident took place due to the negligent act of the deceased only and not due to the rider of Motor Cycle.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
On perusal of these documents, it is clear that the concerned I.O after investigation have filed Charge sheet against rider of Bike bearing No.KA05LC5006 for the alleged offences punishable U/s 279, 304(A) of IPC and U/Sec.181 and 187 of IMV Act for the reason that the rider of Bike had no valid driving licence at (SCCH3) 11 M.V.C.No.5754/2022 the time of accident to ride such type of vehicle.
Further the said rider after causing the accident did not provided first aid treatment to the injured, not informed about the accident to the Police and had not stopped the vehicle and fled away from the accident spot.
So, as per Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 the multiplier applicable is "05" and the same is considered.
In order to prove the income of the deceased, the petitioners have produced Invoice and Bill issued by Onion, Potato merchants and commission agents as per Ex.P.12 and 13, except these documents the petitioners have not produced any other relevant documents or examined the author of these documents to prove that the deceased was earning Rs.50,000/ p.m. Hence in the absence of such,
it is just and proper to consider the income as per Minimum Wages Act by considering the deceased as unskilled worker which comes to Rs.13,311/ p.m. Since the deceased has left two dependents, as per Sarla Varma and others Vs Delhi Transport Corporation and others case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 if the dependents are 2 to 3, then personal deduction is to be 1/3rd.
Hence, in this case 1/3rd deduction has to be done towards personal expenses.
The respondent No.1 has admit the policy and it is in force on the date of accident.
The respondent No.2 being the owner had violated the terms of the policy by allowing the rider of bike to ride it without having driving licence.
It is true that the respondent No.2 has violated the terms (SCCH3) 16 M.V.C.No.5754/2022 of the policy.
But this is not a ground to exonerate the liability fastened on the respondent No.1.
22.
The respondent No.1 has relied upon decision reported in: a. M.F.A.No.6154/2019 - Hemalatha @ Hema @ Hemavathi and others V/s Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd., and another - It is observed that the insured will not be indemnified if the vehicle is used otherwise than in accordance with law.
23.
b. 2019 ACJ 713 - Gurmail singh V/s Bajaj Allianz General insurance Co., Ltd.,  It is observed that the insurance company has to satisfy the award and then to recover the same from the owner.
(SCCH3) 17 M.V.C.No.5754/2022
c. National insurance company V/s Swaran Singh - (2004) 3 SCC 297
d. Pappu V/s Vinod kumar lamba (2018) 3 SCC 208 - It is observed that when there is no driving licence the insurer has to pay compensation to claimants with liberty to recover it from the owner.
Bhimakka vs Cholamandalam General Insurance Co., ... on 15 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/129579109/
7 e.
New India Assurance company V/s Yallavva 2020(2) KCCR 1405 -
Hence in the instant case looking into the facts (SCCH3) 18 M.V.C.No.5754/2022 and circumstances of case the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation eventhough there is no valid driving licence by the offending rider.
opennyai_summary.decision:
The Insurance Company i.e., respondent No.1 has to pay the compensation to the petitioners and then to recover the same from the respondent No.2.
25.
With regard to apportionment is concerned, petitioners No.1 and 2 being the wives of the deceased are equally entitled for 50% each of the amount awarded.
Hence, the issue No.3 is answered in partly affirmative.
26. Issue No.4:
In view of my findings on issues No.1 to 3 as above and with regard to awarding the interest is concerned, the petitioners are entitled for simple interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till deposit.
As such I proceed to pass the following: ORDER
The claim petition filed by the petitioners U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for Rs.6,42,440/ (Six lakhs forty two thousand four hundred and (SCCH3) 19 M.V.C.No.5754/2022 forty only) as compensation with interest at 6% p.a from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
However in view of having valid insurance - the respondent No.1 shall deposit the same within time stipulated under section 168(3) of M.V. Act and then to recover from the respondent No.2.
On deposit of the compensation amount with interest, petitioners No.1 and 2 are equally entitled for 50% each of compensation as awarded.
Out of the share amount of petitioners No.1 and 2 along with interest accrued, entire amount shall be released to them through Epayment on proper identification without any further proceedings.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/.
Draw award accordingly.
